<section_guide number="3" title="Functional Requirements" references="1,2">
<feature_boundaries>
Group requirements by bounded context (consistent business terms and rules), then vertical user
story. Inspect existing repository and deployment shape as separate axes, but never copy technical
layers or service folders into requirement boundaries. Propose grounded context candidates when
missing and clarify only material ambiguity. Preserve this profile's sections, approval and diagram scope.
</feature_boundaries>
<purpose>Propose every user-observable product behavior with evaluable acceptance criteria, then a business-wording context diagram.</purpose>

<questions>
1. Ask only when a protected business decision cannot be safely proposed: which behavior should the product guarantee?
</questions>

<workflow>
Read Sections 1 and 2. Work backward from the intent and business requirements and propose every
functional requirement before asking the user to design one.

Define each as `FR-n` at the start of a heading, list item, or table row, with: actor, starting
situation, business input, applied rules and values with their BR IDs, observable result, related
failure handling (it may name EC IDs that Section 5 defines), Required or Optional, and
Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. Results are user-visible or business-verifiable; never use
screens, widgets, APIs, storage, internal state, technical layers, or impressions. Quality
judgments name a representative situation and the rule that separates adequate from inadequate.
Write each FR so a technical author can derive the technical requirement without another business
question.

After drafting 3.1, generate the `Business Context Diagram`: exactly one Mermaid `C4Context` from
the approved Sections 1-2 and the 3.1 draft. Show target users and business staff by role, this
product as one system, and only the external parties the requirements involve, described by
business responsibility, with business-action relationships. Keep APIs, databases, servers, app
structure, deployment units, and technology names out. Never generate `C4Container` or lower
levels, and never ask an architecture question for it.

When an approved BR changes while drafting, show the affected items in the same digest. Do not
save the Section while an acceptance-changing value or policy is unresolved.
</workflow>

<completion required="true">Confirm every FR and the single Business Context Diagram before saving 3.1-3.2 separately.</completion>
</section_guide>
